LLC.1 Finch LLC was, in turn, controlled by MEB NY Inc., a holding company owned 100% 
directly by Michael Bleich.1 
This classic institutional liability ring-fencing ensures that the bottom-tier operating entity 
interfaces with regulators and prime brokers—absorbing the direct legal risks of high-speed 
trading violations—while the strategic control and ultimate beneficial capital remain vaulted 
within the upper-tier entities.1 Furthermore, Finch LLC served as the direct managing member 
of both Scout Trading and a parallel investment adviser named Ophir Partners LLC.1 Scout 
Trading and Ophir Partners were essentially twin entities operating under common control, 
sharing identical executive leadership.1 
Ophir Partners was registered as an investment adviser with the SEC in 2012, managing 
approximately $24.25 million in client assets.1 However, because Bleich served as the CEO and 
CCO of Ophir Partners, the massive $3 million disciplinary history levied against Scout Trading 
automatically triggered mandatory, permanent disclosures for Ophir.1 The inability to isolate the 
FINRA penalty from the broader organization severely hindered Ophir's ability to pass 
institutional due diligence, contributing to its eventual deregistration and cessation of 
registered advisory activities in 2017.1 
Cayman Islands Master-Feeder Structures and Regulatory Arbitrage 
Following the catastrophic regulatory fallout at Scout Trading and the shuttering of Ophir 
Partners, Bleich transitioned from proprietary broker-dealer operations toward institutional 
discretionary asset management.1 Today, he serves as the Chief Investment Officer of 
Entrypoint Capital, LLC, a firm managing approximately $578 million in regulatory assets under 
management.1 
Entrypoint Capital represents a deliberate evolution in Bleich's corporate structuring, utilizing a 
significantly more robust executive team to potentially insulate the firm from his historical 
regulatory baggage.1 The firm is led by CEO Lawrence Edward Leibowitz, a prominent market 
structure veteran and former COO of the New York Stock Exchange, and Andrew Louis Alkon, 
who serves as CCO, COO, and CFO.1 However, as CIO and indirect owner via Entrypoint 
Partners, LP, Bleich remains the central figure in the firm's alpha generation.1 
To aggregate global capital, Bleich’s enterprises consistently integrate Cayman Islands 
master-feeder structures.1 The "EP Third Moment" strategy—which mathematically seeks to 
exploit the "third moment" or skewness of probability distributions to capture asymmetric 
returns—operates through a complex cross-border architecture.1
